Purpose and Scope  EK.10.67.001 Ground Operations Manual has been prepared to define the management, system, process, resource, etc. documents established and defined to determine and assure the rules of ground operations on the Company’s aircraft as well as the duties and responsibilities of the relevant employee on the basis of the national and international civil aviation legislation and the Company’s regulations. In case of difference between the mandatory implementations and rules of the authorities of the countries where outstations are located and the implementations specified in the manual, the rules and implementations of the relevant countries shall prevail.  EK.10.67.001 Ground Operations Manual is a document issued for the purpose of ensuring compliance with the national and international standards, and covering the practices related to ground operations on board the Company's aircraft.  All Company documents referred herein are accessible in the   Digital Document Management System on Turkish Airlines intranet ( infoportal.thy.com )  This document is issued with the approval of Turkish Airlines Inc. CEO & President.  The ground operations are carried out for the purpose of ensuring airworthiness and continuity of the aircraft in the Company's flight fleet by observing the safety and security rules specified in the manufacturer firm manuals.  0.2. Feasibility  Turkish Airlines certifies that EK.10.67.001 Ground Operations Manual complies with the Republic of Türkiye DGCA and EASA regulations and the requirements of Turkish Airlines Air Operator Certificate (AOC).  EK.10.67.001 Ground Operations Manual is prepared in compliance with “ DK.41.016 IATA Ground Operations Manual (IGOM)”. It is shared with the authorized personnel of contracted ground handling companies through the   Ground Operation Document Monitoring  System for passenger aircraft and   Business Process Management (BPM) for cargo aircraft.  The rules (procedure, work flow, task distributions, etc.) introduced by the manual describe the current ground operation and all the associated operations. EK.10.67.001 Ground Operations Manual has been prepared in accordance with the national and international regulations and the regulations and rules of Turkish Airlines.  0.3. Risk Assessment  The current risk assessments of the Company's Ground Operations are available in the AQD system.  All requirements within the scope of   DK.41.016 IATA Ground Operations Manual (IGOM) Risk Assessments are determined as “Safety Critical” and the risk assessments of the processes are reviewed in each   DK.41.016 IATA Ground Operations Manual (IGOM) revision and possible differences that may occur with the Company ground operation risk assessments are determined by the Ground Operations Safety and Compliance Directorate/Safety Follow-up Directorate for passenger aircraft and by the Cargo Operations Directorate/Cargo Flight Operations Control Management/Safety Tracking Supervisory for cargo aircraft. They are put on the agenda of   the   monthly   Safety   Representatives   Meeting   to   review   the   differences   identified   together   with   the   Company’s   current   risk assessments. After the revision review of all requirements in D K.41.016 IATA Ground Operations Manual (IGOM), a meeting is planned with the same participants and process owner unit representatives, without waiting for the next Safety Representatives meeting, for situations where a risk other than the current Company risks is determined and quick action is required for this risk. In the relevant meeting, in order to reduce the risk levels arising from the risk assessment made as per the business processes detailed in  PR.10.21.007 Procedure for Safety Hazard Identification and Risk Management, an action with a deadline is assigned to the relevant parties via the AQD and put into practice.  The authorizations to make decisions about the safety risks of the ground operations are defined in PR.10.21.007 Procedure for  Safety Hazard Identification and Risk Management and the authorization to make decisions about the security risks in EK.10.15.001  Security Program/article 2.2.   Company Security Organization and Structure.  0.5. Official Language  This document has been prepared in Turkish and translated into English. May/need not/not necessary/not required:   indicates that conformance is optional.  b.Note:   indicates an important point about which the manual user needs to be made aware.  c.Should/if possible/whenever possible:   indicates that conformance is considered optional, but desirable.  d.Shall/must/necessary/need/required:   indicates that conformance is considered mandatory.  e.Shall not/must not:   indicates that something is not allowed/permitted, or is forbidden.  0.6.2. Quotation Usage  The statements in this manual must be used in the verbal and written official uses in their complete forms as defined herein.  0.6.3. Punctuation and Spelling  Bold texts are section headings or include highlighted sentences/words. The texts in quotation marks are technical terms.  0.7. Standard Format  0.7.1. The distribution of EK.10.67.001 Ground Services Manual for cargo aircraft is provided by the Cargo Operations Directorate/Quality and Document Management Directorate through the   Business Process Management (BPM) system. The contact information of the handling companies in the system is kept up-to-date by the cargo operation supervisors, cargo sales supervisors, and the employee assigned by the International Cargo Sales Assistant Directorate under the coordination of the Cargo Handling Agreement Directorate. The follow-up of the receipt information and the elimination of the deficiencies are ensured by the cargo operation supervisors, cargo sales supervisors, and the employee assigned by the International Cargo Sales Assistant Directorate by making the necessary reporting to the international organization under the coordination of the Cargo Handling Management. If distribution cannot be done via the BPM system, distribution is done via e-mail or the Distribution Processes folder. In that case, the firms’ confirmations of receipt of the document are received by e-mail; additionally, through quarterly checks, it is confirmed and assured through   FR.61.0128 Cargo  Operations Monitoring Management And Evaluation Form that the updated versions of the relevant manuals are accessible to firms. EK.10.67.001 The temporary revisions and revised handbook prepared as annexes to the Ground Handling Handbook are uploaded to the BPM system by the Cargo Operations Directorate/Quality and Document Management Supervisory after being published in DDMS (before entering into force) and sent to the Cargo Handling Agreements Director for distribution approval in accordance with the GHA (Ground Handling Agent) list to which the updated documents from the Cargo Handling Agreements Directorate will be forwarded. The said temporary revision and   EK.10.61.003 Cargo Operations Manual, if updated, are sent to all cargo departments (including international) with an announcement in PDF form and with reference to the DDMS link. Bilateral Air Transport Agreements  In order to combine the commercial rights of the international airlines in accordance with a multilateral agreement, the Chicago Convention, which has been executed on 07.12.1944, has been acknowledged as the constitutional law of the civil aviation and has been ratified also by the Republic of Türkiye by virtue of the law numbered 4749 and dated 05.06.1945.  Pursuant to article six of the mentioned convention; two states, that wish to perform and carry out air transport between each other, are free to specifically execute any bilateral agreements. Such agreements are required to be in compliance with the provisions of the mentioned convention and also be registered by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). Bilateral Air Transport Agreements comprise of a main text and an annex or any annexes. The main text comprises of the matters regarding the definitions, traffic rights, fashion of granting of authority to the air operators to be designated by the parties, revocation and/or suspension of the authority, the requirement that the capitals and the actual control activities of the air operators should be in the possession of the citizens of the contracting states, the requirement to comply with the local regulations, no collection of any customs from the other items at the airports, aviation security, provisions, storage of the customary aviation equipment and supplies, information and statistics, consultation, conformance to the multilateral agreements, amendment of the agreement, termination of the agreement, tariff rates, entry into force, etc. E K . 1 0 . 6 7 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 1 6 G r o u n d O p e r a t i o n s M a n u a l ( G O M ) QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 42 | Total Page: 464 Copy of this document has been generated on 4.02.2026 16:42. 1.1.1.2.1. Editing Processes  The flights are created on the DCS System 48 hours before the scheduled time of departure (STD). After creating the flights, the editing processes depending on the schedule structure of the station are carried out 48 to 24 hours before the scheduled time of departure by the station official or the employee assigned by the station official. Passenger on Stretcher (STCR),  c.   Extra Seat (EXST),  d.   Group Passenger,  e.   Dead Head Crew/Technician,  f.   Out-of-order seats that cannot be used,  g.   Un/Accompanied Minor,  h.   Wheelchair-bound passenger (WCHR, WCHS, etc.),  i. Checks to be done before Check-in Procedures),  j.   Deportee/INAD Passenger,  k.   VIP passenger,  l.   Passenger traveling with Assistance Dog,  m.   Passenger left behind due to overbooking.  1.1.1.2.2. Allocation of Seats to Passengers  The details of paid seat allocation in all flights (TK) are available on   www.thy.com.  1.1.1.2.3. General  Check-in is the full order of the steps that include recording of the passengers and baggage in DCS or a manual system, tagging and labeling of the baggage, and issuance of one or more than one boarding passes. The boarding pass that includes the passenger's name must be given to all passengers on paper or in the electronic environment. Check-in waiting times for economy and business class passengers are included in   EK.10.67.008 Ground Operations Quality Manual/4.5. Check-in Counter Application Practices Procedures.  1.1.3.2. Check-in Deadlines  At Company flights, the closure time of check-in processes for domestic flights is 45 minutes, and the closure time of check-in processes for international flights is 60 minutes. In case of flight delay for 30 minutes and longer, the check-in transactions are terminated 45 minutes before a domestic flight or 60 minutes before an international flight on the basis of the new planned departure time. However, in case of differences among the outstations in relation to check-in closure periods, the rules of the authority of the relevant country apply.  1.1.3.3. Operating Carrier, Marketing Carrier, and Wet Lease Check-in Transactions  In codeshare and wet lease flights, if the carrier code mentioned on the ticket is other than the operating carrier, the transactions must be made by giving the passenger information about the operating carrier at the reservation/ticket sale stage.  1.1.3.4. Rules to Consider in Passport Control  a. Check the photograph, date of birth and appearance data on the passport by comparing them with the passenger.  b.   Check the expiry date of the passport.  c.   Check, by looking from both directions at the area where the photograph is stuck, whether the relevant page has been damaged as a result of changing the original photograph.  d.   The stamps on the passport should be read clearly in both directions Check if there is disconnection and change in the points where the stamp and the photograph unite.  e.   Check if there is spelling error, deficient information, deletion and scraping in the passport information.  f.   Check if the signature area of the passport is signed by the passport holder.  g.   Check whether there is any damage on the passport or not. The implied by damage is separation of the passport completely or partially from its cover, sticking the passport to the cover or trying to stitch, separation of the plastic thin layer in the photographed page completely or partially or tearing it, existence of any amendment (date etc.), deletion which is not approved by relevant authorities and other defects.  1.1.5.2.4. Points to consider in Visa Check  a.   Check if the passenger has the visa to the country he/she wants to travel.  b.   Check the start and end dates of the visa which determine its validity. The passenger should travel between these dates.  c.   Visa types must be checked, and primary visa types are as follows:  Airport Transit Visa:   It enables the passenger to just wait in the transit area of the airport where transit pass is made. Passenger is not allowed to get out of the transit area. He should have visa of third country (if necessary) and continuation ticket reserved for the same day. The baggage is tagged from the beginning of the travel to the final destination.  Transit Visa:   It enables the passenger to enter the country where transit pass is made. Passenger may stay at the country as much as the permitted period. Passenger should have visa of third country (if necessary). Passenger may continue his/her travel via land, sea or air way. Touristic Visa:   It is a visa type issued for travel reasons. The round trip ticket should be inquired by the airline according to rules of the traveled country.  Commercial Visa:   The visa type issued when traveling to country for commercial/business reasons.  Residence Visa:   The visa type issued for travels targeting family reunification, marriage, work, education in order to get residency permit out of the country where passenger is a citizen. The passenger may travel with a one way ticket.  Diplomatic Visa:   The visa type issued for those who hold diplomatic passports.  Entry Point Visa:   It is the visa type issued at airport when entering the country by the relevant authority of the country at the destination point in case there is no need for consulate visa.  Electronic Visa:   It is the visa issued by registering the passport number in the electronic environment. There is no visa in the form of tag, ink stamp on the passport before travel.  Exit/Re-entry Visa:   It is the visa type that lets the passenger exit from the country and re-enter it.  d.   While some countries clearly state the visa types on the visas, some countries define the visa types by letters.  e.   The visa types for passengers who travel to Schengen countries should be taken into consideration as follows;  A Type Visa:   It is the airport transit visa and the passenger continues his/her travel by airline and should have a reserved ticket. It enables the passenger to wait in transit lounge. There is no permit to enter the country where transit pass is made.  C Type Visa:   It is the visa type granted for touristic/commercial/transit reasons.  D Type Visa:   It is the visa type given for residency reasons.  f.   Check if the visa is single entry (01), double entry (02) or multiple entry. The points to consider in these controls are as follows;  Single Entry (01) Visa  In order to find out if the passenger has traveled between the start and end dates of the visa, check the entry/exit stamps on the passport. Single entry visas cannot be used again once they have been used.  Double Entry (02) Visa  Double entry visas enable double entry/exit including start and end dates of the visa. The entry/exit stamps in the passport should be checked.  Multiple Entry Visa  It enables the passenger to make limitless entry/exit between the start and end dates of the visa. In case the residency period mentioned on the visa is completed, the visa is deemed invalid even if its dates are valid.  g.   Other than the visas mentioned above, some countries may grant different numbers of entries. In such visas the figure written in the entry number section should be taken into consideration.  h.   Check if there is any deletion, scraping, deficient information or spelling error on the visa.  i.   Check if the children registered in the passport are included in the visa. In case children travel with their parents (according to the destination country), they should definitely be registered in an individual visa or parent visa.  j.   The name/surname on the passport should be same with the name-surname on the visa.  1.1.5.2.5. 1.1.5.3. Advanced Passenger Information System (APIS) Application  APIS application is the act of forwarding special advanced security details of the passengers to the immigration departments of the arrival country through message. APIS is the manifest form covering the details of passengers and passports constituted in accordance with IATA regulations. The practicability of the system is based on ensuring that the messages, comprising of the mentioned details, are automatically sent to the stations of arrival through the DCS, upon completion of the processes pertaining to the routes determined by the authorities. APIS is divided into two categories as edifact transmission application, namely the UN and US APIS. Both applications have different features in respect of form and content.  a. US APIS Application  In respect of such application, it is essential to forward five details regarding the passengers and their passports (DOB: Date of Birth, GEN: Gender, NAT: Nationality, AFN: Name, PPT: Passport Number). If any of this information is missing, the system does not allow issuing boarding passes during the check-in processes carried out at the departure station. Entering this information after check-in in “Through check-in” procedures prevents getting the boarding pass of second flights from the first station and accordingly @B should be performed for the second flight. Therefore; in respect of "through check-in" processes, it is important to enter "API" details prior to check-in processes in order to take any and all actions accurately and quickly. APIS details may be processed on the system automatically by entering the readable passport or visa details through the keyboards, which may read the same, and they shall also be entered to the system manually in case of unavailability of such keyboards.  Manual APIS Entries  APIS entries shall be performed individually or at once while the passenger details are displayed on the screen. At once; 1/AFN/....|PPT.....|NAT.....|GEN/... Or it is entered as follows. 1/AFN/... 1/PPT/... 1/NAT/... 1/GEN/... 1/DOB/…  APIS Cancellations  At once; 1/X/AFN|X/PPT|X/NAT|X/GEN Or it is entered as follows. 1/X/AFN 1/X/PPT 1/X/NAT 1/X/GEN 1/X/DOB  Viewing US APIS Information Lists  They shall be displayed on the UC Mode through the PM/D entry in respect of the relevant flight.  b.UN APIS Application E K . 1 0 . 6 7 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 1 6 G r o u n d O p e r a t i o n s M a n u a l ( G O M ) QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 65 | Total Page: 464 Copy of this document has been generated on 4.02.2026 16:42. d. General  Baggage is the registered or unregistered (cabin/carry-on) clothing and personal items traveling with the passenger.  1.1.6.2. Cabin Baggage  a.General  Any baggage of maximum 8 kg and 23x40x55 cm, which is under the control and supervision of the passenger and carried in the passenger cabin free of charge under the seats in front of the passenger or in the overhead bins. The details related to the cabin baggage handling rules are defined in   TL.60.001 Cabin Baggage Acceptance Instruction. When the occupancy rate in all aircraft types of the Company exceeds 70%, in order to prevent possible flight delays and to facilitate passengers to settle in the cabin, standard cabin baggage is accepted as checked baggage on a voluntary basis during check-in as per the rules in   TL.60.001 Cabin Baggage  Acceptance Instruction with the approval of the station manager.  b. Cabin Baggage Types 1.   The cabin baggage must not be larger than 23x40x55 cm and heavier than 8 kg. If the first degree family members (mother, father, spouse, child, sibling) apply to the check-in counter at the same time in domestic flights, the “POOLED” transaction is made without requiring being in the same reservation. Persons traveling with passengers in special categories of passengers in need of assistance (WCH, minor passenger, young passenger, MAAS passenger, disabled passenger) are POOLED without the requirement of being in the same PNR.  1.1.6.6. Delivery at Aircraft (DAA)  The method with regard to the baggage to be delivered to passengers at the aircraft door in the flights of Company is described below.  a. Feasibility  All passengers to travel and baggage are checked by the relevant law enforcement officers or by the private security units prior to the “boarding” process, and then allowed on the flight. The pushchairs and wheelchairs must be checked in. In cases where a passenger requests to receive his/her baggage at the aircraft door during ground operations, the compliance of the baggage with the gate delivery baggage criteria (pushchair, baby bassinet, wheelchair) is taken into consideration. It is ensured that the door/aircraft delivery baggage are sent to the aircraft and loaded in accordance with the acceptance conditions and loading rules and delivered within the time range and place determined in compliance with the above-said conditions at the destination station.  It is necessary to monitor loading of the door-delivery pushchairs, the wheelchairs and gurneys the passenger will not need in the cabin to the hold. Since the electronic devices, valuable documents, and valuable articles must be accompanied by passenger, DAA procedure must not be applied. These articles are accepted to the cabin together with the passenger, not carried in the cargo compartment. However, the carry-on baggage must meet the cabin baggage dimensions.  b. Boarding Gate Procedure  The baggage to which no cabin baggage tag has been attached at the boarding lounge is checked; and any cabin baggage without tag must not be allowed in the passenger cabin. Application details regarding cabin baggage are described in   article 1.1.6.2. Cabin Baggage.  In case of detection of any passengers, requesting their baggage to be delivered at door/aircraft, during the boarding process, then it shall be checked that whether proper tagging and packaging have been performed, or not. Detailed information about implementation is available in   TL.67.065 Instruction on Delivery Baggage at Aircraft Door. If the manual boarding transaction shall be made, it is ensured that the passengers show their baggage at hold in order for the baggage reconciliation. Manual "checklist" shall be drawn up in order to detect any missing passengers. In case of any missing passenger, then it shall be ensured that the announcement is performed. In the event that the passenger does not apply, then the operations department shall be informed in order to offload the baggage.  The passenger and the items carried in their luggage must be checked to ensure that they comply with the requirements of DK.41.011  Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR)/2.3. Dangerous Goods Carried by Passengers or Crew.It must be ensured that the articles especially prohibited to carry in the cargo compartment are removed from the baggage.  It is necessary to ensure that the baggage pieces brought together at the boarding gate to be loaded into the cargo compartment are tagged, and the load control department is informed so that they consider the collected carry-on baggage pieces during the Weight and Balance calculations. Carriage of Wheelchairs and Other Mobility Aids  In order to prevent damage to the aircraft and to ensure flight safety, electric wheelchairs and other mobility devices may be carried on passenger aircraft with the approval of the Association for wheelchairs and other mobility devices powered by lithium batteries, wet or dry batteries, in accordance with the requirements set out in   DK.41.011 Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR)/2.3.   Dangerous Goods Carried by Passengers or Crew. The following processes are carried out during acceptance of the same: When   battery-powered   wheelchair   or   other   mobility   aids   are   carried   on   the   flight,   the   pilot-in-command   is   informed   of location/position of the same. When they are removed from the wheelchairs or other mobility aids, the carriage location/position of the batteries are informed to the pilot-in-command. For the purposes of avoiding undesired situations and protecting the equipment while stowing and securing the wheelchairs or other mobility aids, it is ensured that they will not be damaged by the movements of cargoes, mails, and baggage. The load control department must know that there are electric mobility equipment on the flight. In order to ensure that the wheelchair is delivered to the passenger as soon as possible, a message shall be sent to the destination or the transfer station. The message must include the name and seat number of the passenger, the position of the wheelchair, and the position of the battery that must have been removed from the wheelchair.  Wheelchair:   Two (2) motion mechanisms are carried in the free cargo compartment together with the baggage that contains the equipment. Wheelchairs/handicapped mobility aids can be accepted outside of the standard baggage weight and dimensions. If the wheels of the wheelchair are separate from the chair, they are accepted as wheelchair equipment, and no extra baggage fee is collected. However, wheelchair/handicapped mobility aid dimensions must be checked to be suitable with the aircraft compartment door measurements. If it is requested that more than two wheelchairs/handicapped mobility aids be carried, the process will be carried out within the passenger's free baggage allowance. In acceptance of the wheelchairs which operate with dry, liquid, and lithium battery, the responsibility of disconnecting/de-energizing the batteries belongs to the passengers and/or accompanying persons. The assigned ground handling agent employee receiving the wheelchair is responsible for checking that the battery is disconnected/de-energized. Acceptance of Non-Spillable (Dry) Battery Wheelchairs/Other Mobility Aids  The other battery-powered mobility aids are tied down by using straps or secured by taking other safety measures. The other mobility aids, batteries, electric cables, and control cables must be protected against potential damage that may be caused by movements of baggage, mails, or cargoes. The wheelchairs or other mobility aids must be informed in advance; the equipment that meets the Company's procedures are carried. The features the equipment is expected to have are specified below. The passenger is required to confirm that the battery s/he will deliver is a non-spillable liquid battery or nickel-hydride battery or dry battery, which meets   DK.41.011 Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR) special condition A67. The non-spillable batteries must also meet   DK.41.011 Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR) Package Instruction 872 special condition/requirement. Battery terminals must be insulated to prevent accidental short circuits. (For example: The battery can be insulated by being kept in the container.) Each battery also: The electric circuits of the wheelchair or other mobility aids are insulated safely as per the manufacturer's instructions. If the wheelchair or other mobility aid requested to be accepted to the aircraft is custom production, the battery shall be removed by the passenger. Each passenger may carry only one spare battery. If a specially produced non-spillable (dry) battery needs to be removed from a wheelchair or other mobility device to be transported in the cargo compartment, the batteries are transported in safe and sturdy packages. The location/position of other motion devices and filled batteries, removed batteries and spare batteries must be notified to the pilot- in-command in writing (on the Loadsheet in accordance with   LS.67.051 Table of Dangerous Goods Passengers and Crew are  Allowed to Carry with Them). The wheelchairs or the other mobility aids powered by sealed battery must be secured against the movements in the cargo department and carried as protected against damage from movements of the baggage, mails, and the other cargoes. If the wheelchairs and the other sealed battery mobility aids are designed in such a manner as to allow removing the battery, The battery must be separated from the vehicle. In that case, the wheelchair or the other sealed battery mobility aids may be carried as checked baggage without any restriction. If the battery will be removed, the removed battery must be carried in the cargo hold in a solid and hard package. The battery must be protected against short circuits.  4. Acceptance of Liquid (Spillable) Battery Wheelchairs/Other Mobility Aids  Wheelchairs or other spillable battery mobility aids are specified in the requirements of   DK.41.011 Dangerous Goods Regulations  (DGR)/2.3.   Dangerous Goods Carried by Passengers or Crew as follows. The batteries and the other mobility aids are tied down by using straps or secured by taking other safety measures. The other mobility aids, batteries, electric cables, and control cables must be protected against potential damage that may be caused by movements of baggage, mails, or cargoes. Wheelchairs or other battery-powered mobility devices; those with leakage-prone (liquid) batteries: For the loading of wheelchairs or other similar mobility devices powered by leakage-prone (liquid) batteries for the use of disabled passengers, passengers with temporary mobility problems (e.g. leg fractures), or passengers who are ill or elderly; wheelchairs or other mobility devices with leakage-prone (liquid) batteries are carried on flights provided that the following conditions are met: Batteries must be insulated to prevent short circuits that may occur. (Battery can be insulated by keeping it in a container.) The batteries must be carried together with spill-resistant ventilation caps as far as possible. 1.1.7.3. Passenger Discrepancy in Boarding  The requirements related to passenger count in cabin are defined in   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A/8.2.2.1.5.   Passenger Count and   EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew Manual/article 8.1.14. Passenger Count. On the domestic and international flights that park next to boarding bridge, have “gate reader” application, and reconcile passengers and baggage, the passenger count in cabin is not performed. In cases where these requirements are not met, or at the airports listed in   LS.15.021 List of Countries’ Risk Ratings and deemed risky in consequence of the risk assessments made by Security Directorate, even if these requirements are met, the passengers are counted. On board the aircraft parked in the remote parking positions, and on the transit flights whose passengers wait inside the cabin, the passengers are counted absolutely. The requirements to be met when the passengers stay on board the aircraft at the transit stops are given in   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A/8.2.2.1.5.   Passenger Count and EK.10.71.001 Cabin Crew  Manual/10.2.9 Security Measures for the Hand Baggage Left on Board at Transit Airports. In the following cases after completion of passenger boarding, the passenger count in cabin is not conducted on any of the Company's domestic and international flights parked next to boarding bridge. The boarding official checks that the passenger list in the check-in system matches the information of the passengers boarding the aircraft, and that an agreement has been reached on the number of passengers. During this check, the passengers' boarding passes are checked for identification and had scanned by the “gate reader”. It is necessary to make sure that the flight number, date, route, passenger name and seat number on the boarding pass match the information in the check-in system. When the boarding pass has been scanned by the “gate reader”, if the system warns that this match has not been achieved, the passenger is not let board the aircraft unless the relevant error is corrected. (The information on the boarding pass of the passenger boarding the aircraft and the information recorded in the check-in system must be identical.) The screenshots of the mobile boarding passes must be obtained by having them scanned by the “gate reader” device. The passenger let in the aircraft/passenger lounge after the information on the passenger "boarding" and the answer received from the system after the passenger has "boarded" match each other, and a boarding pass is generated for the passenger passing with mobile boarding pass and added to the passes. The boarding passes of all passengers passing through the passenger lounges must be had scanned by the “gate reader” devices. The passengers who have not applied to the “boarding” gate must be “offloaded” from DCS before completion of “boarding”, and if they have baggage, their baggage must be sorted out, and the “boarding” process must be completed by informing the number of passengers who have boarded the aircraft to the ground operations employee acting as the Operations Coordinator and/or the flight crew. In addition to these measures, the unauthorized persons are not allowed to enter and exit through the service and rotunda doors of boarding bridges; the station official is responsible for taking the necessary preventive actions. During boarding of the passengers, at the aircraft door, the cabin crew looks at the seat numbers on the passenger parts of the boarding passes for the purpose of directing them to their seats in the cabin. If any passenger who does not have the “boarding pass” issued for the relevant flight is at the boarding bridge service door, the cabin chief of the flight informs the passenger services/ground operations employee acting as the Operations Coordinator of the situation.  The requirements regarding the security measures to be taken for passengers who board the aircraft incorrectly/cancel flying are defined in the articles   EK.10.15.001 Security Program/3.5. Passengers Who Cancel Flying/Passengers Who Board the Aircraft By  Mistake, EK.10.73.001   Operations https://ddms.thy.com/OPEN/EK.10.71.001/TR/%23PAGE%3D239/ Manual Part-A andEK.10.71.001  Cabin Crew Handbook/10.2.10.Security Measures to be Taken for Passengers Who Board the Aircraft By Mistake or Cancel Flying.  The number of passengers informed when the “boarding” process is over and the number of passengers specified in the “Load Sheet” must be the same. For the passenger(s) who have not applied to the “boarding”, the necessary Last Minute Changes (LMC) must have been made on the “Load Sheet” by the ground operations employee acting as the Operations Coordinator. After performing the baggage reconciliation process on board the aircraft by using the baggage reconciliation system, the aircraft is closed without counting. After completion of the passenger boarding process, the cabin crew and the station official agree on that the processes have been completed perfectly, thus ensuring that the aircraft is closed without counting the passengers as per the requirements of EK.10.71.001  Cabin Crew Manual/article 8.1.14. Passenger Count. In the event that the authorized ground operations employee, or the cockpit or cabin crew doubts the abovementioned processes have not been completed perfectly and/or it is found out that any one of the specified processes is incomplete, the cockpit or the station official request the cabin crew to perform a passenger count, and if agreement is reached after the passenger count, the aircraft is closed. In the event that it is found out that there are missing/excess passengers on board the aircraft after the passenger counting, then the boarding official checks identity cards against the passenger list. The missing/excess passenger shall be identified. In case of any baggage pertaining to the missing passenger, then it shall be ensured that it will be "offloaded" from the aircraft. In case excess passenger is detected, the reason is researched and procedures are followed according to decision of station officer. Transfer Passengers  The passengers, who continue their flights by the same airline or another airline, upon stopping at any intermediate station within a period of 24 hours, from the station of origin to the final destination, provided that they have a confirmed ticket.  a.   The baggage of the passengers shall be checked-in until the final destination by taking into account the customs regulations, provided that baggage, confirmed tickets and flight routes of the passengers are issued on the same ticket. The same regulation shall be applicable to the Star Alliance member airlines. However; In the event that the flight routes (TK-TK) of any passenger have been ticketed individually, and that there is a time interval of minimum two (2) hours and maximum 24 hours between the relevant flight and the connection flight, then the baggage shall be tagged until the final destination in accordance with the customs regulations and below-mentioned procedures will be realized: Check-in procedure is realized via the second flight record and BSM should be formed by entering baggage tag numbers as k- edit in the check-in record. If the passenger has excess baggage, the fee should be collected from first destination point until the last point where the baggage is tagged. In the event that the flight routes to be traveled by any passenger have been ticketed individually, and that the relevant flights will be operated by two different airlines (TK - foreign airline), then, the baggage shall not be tagged until the final destination. Exceptionally; in respect of the HKG, ICN, SIN, NRT, KIX, BKK, PVG, CAN and KUL flights of the Company, the baggage of the passengers, having connection flights to Taiwan (TPE-KHH-RMQ) and the Philippines (MNL) through any foreign airline, shall be tagged until the final destination.  b.   The station of origin shall definitely carry out the passport and visa checking processes in respect of the connecting flight of the passenger.  c.   In the event that the flight of any passengers ends at any outstation, then the international transfer tag (green color) shall be affixed to their baggage, regardless of the fact that station of origin of such passengers are either domestic or outstation.  d.   In the event that the station of origin of the passengers is any outstation, and that such passengers have a connection flight to any  custom-bound   domestic station within the borders of the Republic of Türkiye, then the domestic transfer tags (orange color) shall be affixed to their baggage.  e.   In the event that the station of origin of the passengers is any outstation, and that such passengers have a connection flight to any  customs-free   domestic station within the borders of the Republic of Türkiye, then no yellow or green transit transfer tags shall be affixed to their baggage, and such baggage shall be tagged until the station of the first entry to the Republic of Türkiye. Passengers shall be necessarily informed, during check-in, regarding the fact that their baggage is required to be cleared at the first custom-bound station in accordance with the customs regulations.  1.3.3.2. Visually and Hearing Impaired Passengers  For the visually-impaired or hearing-impaired passengers, medical report is not necessary. For the visually-impaired or hearing-impaired passengers, it is not necessary to complete   FR.67.0425 Release and Waiver of Liability Form. The visually-impaired or hearing- impaired passengers may travel without company. It is necessary to make sure that the correct SSR entries have been made in DCS and PNR.  1.4.4.2.2. Special Categories of Passengers (SCPs)  They are the passengers who travel as subject to special carriage rules throughout the flight and/or need special support, help and/or equipment; and the term covers at least the following categories of passengers: Persons with Reduced Mobility (PWD), Infants and unaccompanied minors (UM), Deportees, Inadmissible passengers (INAD-Inadmissible), Detainees, Persons subject to Judicial and Administrative Proceedings, and their escorts. If (2) or more SCPs travel together, the seat next to the SCP who needs a companion shall not be left unaccompanied. If the passenger who will accompany the SCP meets the "companion passenger" criteria (not SCP, no other passenger s/he is responsible for in the cabin, etc.) to help the SCP in case of abnormal situations and emergencies and sits next to the SCP, more than one SCP can travel. The companion passenger is the passenger who is physically capable of carrying the SCP to the nearest exist either by lifting or dragging during an emergency/evacuation (without needing a Cabin Crew Member's help). Before boarding, the accompanying passenger is briefed by the ground employee on the special condition of the SCP concerned and the companion passenger’s responsibilities.  1.4.4.3. Allocation of Seats  Special category passengers (SCP) are not permitted to sit on the seats that provide direct access to emergency exits. Besides, the following must be taken into consideration while determining these persons' seats ( DK.33.001 EASA Air Operations Regulations CAT.OP.MPA.155,   DK.22.115 SHT-OPS | Instruction on the Procedures and Principles for Flight Operations/NCO.IDE.A.140.): They must not prevent the cabin crews from performing their duties. They must not block the access to emergency equipment, or They must not prevent the emergency evacuation. Passengers who require Medical Permission  1.4.5.1. General  In the event that any passengers declare at the check-in counter that they are sick, then   FR.67.0423 Incapacitated Passenger Medical Information Sheet shall be completed, and such passengers shall be referred to health-care organization in the event that medical doctor's report is required. In cases where the passenger becomes ill and needs to be disembarked from the aircraft, FR.67.0122  Declaration Form for Denied Passengers is prepared by the station official. The detailed activities to be carried out in this regard are explained in   TL.10.67.004 General Instruction on Admittance of Disabled and Sick Passengers. At the Izmir, Ankara, Antalya, and Istanbul stations affiliated to Ground Operations Directorate, the procedures are carried out within the framework of the processes detailed in   PR.67.087 Procedure For Sick Passenger Processes.  1. Medical Doctor's Report a.   Medical doctor's report shall have been obtained within the last 10 days.  b.   Such report shall have been written on the letterhead of the medical doctor or health-care organization.  c.   Date of issue of the report shall be necessarily specified. The full name, diploma number and signature of the medical doctor, who has issued the report, shall be necessarily specified on the report.  d.   In case of the sick passengers or passengers with partially or completely reduced mobility who have medical report due to their status, such reports must be checked completely by the check-in official. Medical doctor's reports shall bear the expression   "The passenger is fit to travel by air" . Such report shall not be older than 10 days as of the date of issue, and shall have been issued either in Turkish or English. In order for medical doctor’s reports issued in the languages other than Turkish or English to be valid, the passengers are made sure to travel after the related employee translates the expression   “The passenger is fit to travel by air”   and indicates their first/last name together with their title, and signs the medical doctor's report. In the event that the relevant employee is the employee of the ground handling agent, then the abovementioned practice shall be carried out by the employee of the ground handling agent, and it shall also be ensured that such passengers will travel upon the approval of the Company’s employee.  e.   In the event that it is specified on the medical report, the relevant passengers travel as accompanied. Sick passengers shall not be accompanied by the cabin crew members.  f.   One copy of the report shall be filed at the station.  2. Passengers not to be admitted to Flights of the Company even if they have Medical Doctor's Report  a.   The passengers, who are required to use electrical or pneumatic tools during the flight (excluding oxygen cylinder and portable respiratory equipment provided by the Company),  b.   The passengers, who have suffered from asthma attack before the aircraft doors are closed,  c.   The infants born within the last 48 hours,  3. Passengers to be admitted to Flights of the Company with Medical Doctor's Report  a.   The passengers who declare that they have suffered from any kind of cardiac diseases, vascular diseases, chest diseases, and brain diseases as well as any surgical operations (by-pass, angiography, cardiac surgery, brain surgery, etc.) as a result of such diseases in the last three (3) months or who make a special request shall be admitted to the flight with a medical doctor’s report bearing the expression   “The passenger is fit to travel by air” .  b.   The passengers who suffer from respiratory failure as a result of asthma and other chronic pulmonary diseases, cardiac diseases as well as the ones who will travel with medical supports such as catheter, drain, etc. are admitted to the flight with a medical report bearing the expression   “The passenger is fit to travel by air” . The details are available in PR.67.021  Procedure for Applications Related to Disabled Passengers or Passengers with Reduced Mobility.  c. Handling  In case of rejection of PWD and/or passenger who requests MEDA, the employee informs the passenger of the reason why s/he is rejected from the flight and explains the reason of rejection by referring to the general rules of carriage. Rules regarding Carriage and Use of Portable Breathing Devices by Passengers in Cabin  The Portable Breathing Devices are divided into three categories as follows:  1- Portable Oxygen Concentrators-(POC)  2- Respiratory Devices (RESPIRATORS, VENTILATORS)  3- Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machines. The passengers who are going to travel with portable breathing devices are required to inform the reservation department of the carriage and/or use of the said devices 48 hours before the flight time. If the passenger declares that they will use a portable breathing device in the cabin, a doctor's report is required.  a. Rules regarding Carriage of Portable Breathing Devices in Cabin with Passengers/Cargo Compartment  The Portable Breathing Devices are carried free of charge either in the cabin, with passengers, or in the cargo compartment. There are no restrictions (FAA approval, brand name, etc.) against carriage of these devices with passengers.  b. Rules regarding the Use of Portable Breathing Devices on Aircraft by Passengers:  In order that POC and breathing devices can be used during the flight (except taking off and landing phases), such devices must be FAA-approved ones or of brands specified in   LS.67.025 List of Portable Oxygen Concentrators (POC). Inadmissible Passengers (INAD)  The information regarding INAD and Deporte (DEPA/DEPU) passengers regarding transit, transfer and arrival stations and the information shared with the airline with whom the flight is made in the scope of a codeshare agreement are described in EK.10.15.001  Security Program/3.9.5.1.   Passengers Not Accepted (INAD).  a.   The passengers who are not allowed to enter any country by the authorities of the relevant country although all travel documents are valid, shall be considered as INAD passengers.  b.   Stations of departure shall be obliged to take any and all required measures in order to prevent any INAD cases. Relevant measures; Any passengers, who are suspected to dispose their passports during the flight, are required to travel upon delivering their passports to the cabin chief of the relevant flight; and the message in relation to informing the stations of arrival about the passports delivered to the cabin chief, are definitely required to be sent to the   KZ/KK/KO/KI   and QISTCVTK telex addresses of such stations. The list of passengers and the list of passengers having connection flights are required to be checked. Any measures required to check the travel documents are required to be taken (ultraviolet devices, magnetic readers, etc.). In respect of any travels for touristic purposes, the requirement for round-trip tickets (R/T) is required to be sought. TIMATIC is required to be checked.  1.4.9.1.1. General  a.   The inbound carrier which brings INAD passengers shall be responsible for returning such passengers.  b.   The INAD passenger is sent back in compliance with the requirements of DK.31.027 ICAO Annex-9/ CHAPTER 5. INADMISSIBLE PERSONS AND DEPORTEES within the rules of the relevant country.  c.   Accordingly, the document, which states the reasons for not allowing the relevant passengers to enter the country by the authorities of the relevant country, shall be submitted to the cabin crew members of the flight together with all documents (ticket, passport,  FR.67.0253 INAD Passenger Undertaking Formetc.) of such passengers.  d.   The inbound carrier is required to provide any bookings of the INAD passengers in respect of the return route or routes.  e.   In the event that the passenger, who is not allowed to enter the country, has tickets for the return route, then it shall be ensured that such passenger will return regardless of the restrictions available on his/her ticket, in accordance with the requirements of DK.41.014  Passenger Services Conference Resolution Manual (PSCRM)/Resolution 701 article 2.1. “Restrictions Waived due INAD” information must be entered in the “Endorsements/Restrictions” section of the ticket.  f.   In the event that INAD passenger has no return ticket, then it shall be ensured that such passenger will purchase ticket. In the event that the passenger cannot afford to purchase ticket, then the inbound carrier, which brings such passenger to the station where the passenger is considered as INAD, shall issue   FR.67.0253 INAD Passenger Undertaking Form, and shall have the form signed by such passenger, and shall issue ticket for such passenger against letter of undertaking.  g.   There are no limitations regarding the number of INAD passengers to be carried at the flights of the Company. INAD passengers shall be boarded primarily, and shall be disembarked upon disembarkation of all passengers, if possible. The detailed information on the travels of deportee passengers is available in   PR.67.014 Procedure for Deportee Transport.  a. Unaccompanied Deportee (DEPU)  Any unaccompanied deportee passenger. On domestic flights, DEPU passengers exceeding 10 passengers on narrow-body aircraft and 20 passengers on wide-body aircraft will be transported with escorts, regardless of their nationality, even if they are considered risk- free.  b. Accompanied Deportee (DEPA)  Any accompanied Deportee passenger. The pilot-in-command shall be entitled not to admit Deportee passengers, who fail to comply with the regulations, and who are considered to disturb any other passengers or to jeopardize flight security. In such cases, escorts shall be requested. Escorts shall be provided by the authorities of the concerned country.  c. Voluntary Repatriate Passenger (VR Passenger)  The passenger who has entered the country legally or illegally and is being deported by the competent authorities of the country legally, and voluntarily of his own will. The passenger is enabled to travel as per the processed detailed in TL.67.084 Instruction on Istanbul  Station Voluntary Repatriate (Deportee) Passenger Transactions. On domestic flights, VR Passenger passengers exceeding 10 passengers on narrow-body aircraft and 20 passengers on wide-body aircraft will be transported with escorts, regardless of their nationality, even if they are considered risk-free.  1.4.9.2.1. Booking processes of Deportee passengers shall be carried out by the authorities of the relevant country.  c.   The pilot-in-command and the cabin chief shall be informed about Deportee passengers.  d.   There are no limitations regarding the number of Deportee passengers to be carried at the flights of the Company.  e.   Deportee passengers shall be boarded primarily, and shall be disembarked upon disembarkation of all passengers, if possible.  f. The stations of departure shall send PSM (Passenger Service Message) for Deportee passengers to KZ/KK/KO/KI and ISTCVTK addresses of the stations of transfer, transit and arrival through the message format specified under article 1.4.9.1.1. General Conditions of Passenger Transportation  Any passengers, who act aggressively, threateningly, dangerously, disrespectfully, negligently and disruptively in a manner to jeopardize the security of the ground and flight (cockpit/cabin crew members) employee and/or the passengers, and to cause loss of life and/or property, and to damage aircraft or crew equipment, and to prevent the employee from carrying out their duties or to cause their performances to be impaired, and to affect safe and efficient operation negatively, and/or who insist on acting in breach of the instructions of the Company, and any kinds of regulations required to be followed legally, as well as the instructions given by the relevant employee on the basis of such regulations. The principal goal of the Company is to ensure safe, secure, relaxing and comfortable travel of the passengers and take the necessary measures to achieve this pursuant to the relevant national and international laws, regulations, ordinances and agreement principles as well as the Company's own rules throughout the period from the check-in stage to the arrival station. In order to achieve the above-mentioned objective, in the event that a passenger or a group of passengers are considered inappropriate for boarding due to exhibiting behaviors (dull gaze, loss of ability to think, illogical sentences, stumbling or falling, inability to stand upright, impaired gait, late answers to questions, etc.) indicate that they are under the influence of excessive alcohol and/or under the influence of psychoactive substances on the ground (with the aircraft door open), before the flight/inside the aircraft or act in a way that disturbs the peace and comfort of other passengers due to their unruly behavior, the Company refuses to carry the passenger or passengers in question in order not to jeopardize flight safety. Steps to follow in case of refusal of transport are described in article 1.4.10.2. Processes regarding Unruly Passengers on Ground. The pilot-in-command shall be entitled to take measures and actions for ensuring safety and order on board the aircraft, and to give orders and instructions to the passengers, employee, and any other persons available on board the aircraft for such purpose, and to disembark the persons, who disrupt safety and order, if and when required, in accordance with the authority granted by the international conventions, national and international civil aviation regulations, any other international agreements, contracts and conventions. Any potential verbal or physical attack by any passenger(s) to the Company’s employee is unacceptable. The ground employee and cabin crew members, who encounter any unruly behaviors, shall be supported by the Company in respect of the practices to be performed by the same. The expenses such as transportation, accommodation, food, etc. incurred while any third persons (such as passengers), who undersign the unruly passenger reports as witnesses, are at the police station, prosecution office and/or courts, shall be borne by the Company.  1.4.10.2. Processes regarding Unruly Passengers on Ground  The processes regarding passengers acting unruly during the check-in and boarding phases are given below.  a.   The passenger is warned verbally by the relevant employee. In the event that such verbal warning has been effective and sufficient, then no further actions are required to be taken.  b.   In respect of the passenger insisting on exhibiting unruly behaviors as specified in article 1.4.10.5. Unruly Behaviors despite the verbal warning, the relevant employee ceases the ongoing transaction, and informs the station official about the matter.  c.   In respect of the passengers requiring the response of the law enforcement officers, the check-in official ceases the existing action, and informs the station official about the matter. The station official has   FR.67.0117 Unruly Passenger Ground Incident Report issued. 1.4.10.9.1. Reports to be used during Incidents  a.   The pre-flight and the in-flight final warning reports shall be issued by the flight crew members in 4 copies, in Turkish and English. The first copy shall be submitted to the Flight Operations Directorate; the second copy shall be submitted to the Cabin Crew Directorate; the third copy shall be submitted to the Station Management/Supervisor's Office (to the Station Management/ Supervisor's Office of the airport landed in case of occurrence of the incident during the flight); and the fourth copy shall be submitted to the passenger.  b.   FR.73.0031 On-Board Unruly Passenger Report (On The Ground/In-Flight) is issued in four (4) copies. The first copy is submitted to Flight Operations Directorate, the second copy to Cabin Crew Directorate, the third copy to the Station Management or Ground Operations Directorate; and the fourth copy is given to the passenger.   FR.73.0066 On-Ground/In-Flight Incident Report is issued in five (5) copies. The first copy shall be submitted to the Law Enforcement Officers/Police Officers; the second copy shall be submitted to the Ground   Operations   Directorate/Flight   Operations   Directorate;   the   third   copy   shall   be   submitted   to   the   Ground   Operations Directorate/Cabin Crew Directorate; the fourth copy shall be submitted to the Station Management; and the fifth copy shall be submitted to the passenger.  1.4.10.9.2. Assessment of Reports  The originals of the reports are kept at the relevant station (at the departure station if the incident occurred at the departure station, and at the landing or departure station if it happened inside the aircraft) by the employee or the station official who prepared  FR.67.0117   Unruly   Passenger   Ground   Incident   Report ,   FR.73.0031   On-Board   Unruly   Passenger   Report   (On   The   Ground/In-  Flight)and/or   FR.73.0066 On-Ground/In-Flight Incident Report.  The reporting requirements that must be met in case of security and safety issues on board the aircraft are available in EK.10.73.001  Operations Manual Part-A/10.2.2.4. Reporting Procedure.  1.4.11. Carriage of Persons Subject to Judicial or Administrative Proceedings and of Their Armed Guards  a.   The organization, which has assumed the obligations of the persons subject to judicial or administrative proceedings, shall inform the airline officials about the planned travel, any details for the person to be carried, and the fact that whether such person is considered as dangerous, or not, at least 24 hours prior to the flight, in order to ensure that such persons will travel.  b.   The airline officials must complete   FR.67.0391 Travel Form for Person Subjected to Legal/Administrative Proceedings or Voluntary  Repatriate Passenger for the people subjected to legal or administrative proceedings.  c.   The airline shall not admit any person who is subject to judicial or administrative proceedings without submission of a statement indicating acknowledgment and approval of the related authorities and other companies that are involved in transportation of the criminal until the final destination (including the final destination).  d.   In the event that the person/persons subject to judicial or administrative proceedings is/are considered as dangerous, then maximum one dangerous passenger, for whom administrative or judicial proceedings have been initiated, shall be allowed to travel at a flight.  e.   In the event that the persons subject to administrative or judicial proceedings are considered to have the potential to jeopardize the flight security, by the organization, which has assumed the obligations of such persons, then the airline shall be entitled to reject to carry the persons subject to administrative or judicial proceedings and their escorts.  f.   In the event that the persons subject to administrative or judicial proceedings are considered as non-dangerous by the organization, which has assumed the obligations of such persons, then each person shall be accompanied by at least one law enforcement officer; and in the event that they are considered as dangerous by the same, then they are accompanied by at least two law enforcement officers.  g.   Escorts accompanying the persons subject to the judicial or administrative proceedings shall be obliged to introduce themselves to the safety and security employee as well as to the cabin crew members. The pilot-in-command shall be informed about the persons subject to judicial or administrative proceedings, who will be carried on board the aircraft, as well as the persons accompanying the same and the seat numbers of such persons.  h.   The escorts shall be responsible for removal of any kinds of tools, items or materials, which are carried by the passengers and may be used as weapon by the same, and/or which may jeopardize the flight safety, as well as any kind of flammable items (matches, lighters, etc.), from the persons subject to judicial or administrative proceedings, prior to the flight.  i.   The Company fulfills the requirements set forth in international and national documents regarding the carriage of armed persons and their weapons in the cabin, as well as the rules and regulations of the Company. The Company does not allow carriage of firearms inside the cabin. The detailed information on the implementation is available in   EK.10.15.001 Security Program/article 3.11.   Carriage of Firearms and Ammunition. j. Acceptance and Transfer of Weapons for Armed Guards, Public Security Officers and Passengers  The Company shall implement the provisions set out in the national and international documents regarding carriage of armed persons and their weapons in the cabin. The Company does not allow carriage of firearms inside the cabin. However, the armed persons may exceptionally be allowed to carry weapon with them in the cabin, provided that permission of the competent public institution has been obtained on legal basis, and that the identity card with photograph is submitted. Turkish Airlines shall carry out the following matters.  a.   The gun license of the passenger who will travel armed must be examined by the contracted ground handling employee at the gun delivery desk. Such license shall include the portrait photograph of the armed person, the signature of the official granting permission and the official seal of the service to which the armed person reports.  b.   Any details regarding the full name, seat and status of the person on board the aircraft, e.g. “armed person”, “accompanying person”, “armed person traveling with the arrested person”, etc., must be reported to the pilot-in-command by the contracted ground handling agent employee acting as operations coordinator verbally.  c.   The local procedures that will allow establishing coordination between the ground handling employee and the ramp and operation employee must be set out to ensure that the pilot-in-command is informed prior to leaving the gate/boarding bridge.  d.   In the event that the accompanying persons are armed, then they shall keep the safety lock on.  e.   Local authorities shall be informed about each of the armed security officers, who will be on board the aircraft during the flight, minimum 24 hours prior to take-off or immediately after the Company is informed about the carriage of any armed security officer on board the aircraft within a period of 24 hours. Such information shall cover the ID details of each armed security officer, the travel program and the identification of weapons carried. The declaration of the passengers shall be taken as basis in respect of the pregnancy period and the passengers shall be nicely asked about how many weeks pregnant they are and how many babies they expect.  b.   The passengers who are 28-35 weeks pregnant (beginning of the 28th week and end of the 35th week) and who expect one baby, are allowed to travel through the report, which they have obtained from their own medical doctor, and which bears the expression  "The passenger is fit to travel by air" . The passengers, who are 36 weeks and more pregnant, are not allowed to travel even if they have obtained medical doctor's report. (Table-12: Table for Pregnant Passengers)  c.   The passengers who are 28-31 weeks pregnant (beginning of the 28th week and end of the 31st week) and who expect two or more children, are allowed to travel through the report, which they have obtained from their own medical doctor, and which bears the expression   "The passenger is fit to travel by air" . The passengers, who are 32 weeks and more pregnant, are not allowed to travel even if they have obtained medical doctor's report. (Table-12: Table for Pregnant Passengers) In cases where the passengers travel by connection flights, the passenger must be regarded as accepted to the flight by our Company even if s/he is connecting passenger; and no document must be demanded again for acceptance of that passenger to the flight at the intermediate station. The station official shall make the final decision on continuation of the travels of the passengers who have come from the station of origin of the flight to the intermediate station, depending on the passenger's condition.  d.   In the event that the passengers declare that they suffer from bleeding or pain, then it is necessary to state that the flight may pose risk to their babies and their own health, and request such passengers to consult their medical doctors and obtain medical report accordingly.  e.   Such report shall be issued by any specialist in the relevant matter.  f.   The medical doctor's report shall have been obtained   within the last seven days before the flight date .  g.   Such report shall have been issued on the letterhead of the medical doctor or healthcare organization.  h. Date of issue of the report shall be necessarily specified.  i. The full name, diploma number and signature of the medical doctor, who has issued the report, shall be necessarily specified on the report.  j.   The report shall have been issued in Turkish or English. In order for medical doctor’s reports issued in the languages other than Turkish or English to be valid, the passengers are made sure to travel after the related employee translates the expression   “The passenger is fit to travel by air”   and indicates their first/last name together with their title, and signs the medical doctor's report. In the event that the relevant employee is the employee of the ground handling agent, then the abovementioned practice is carried out by the employee of the ground handling agent; and the first signature is affixed by the employee of the ground handling agent as the issuing person, and then is approved by the employee of the Company; and it is ensured that the passengers travel upon affixing the second signature. Regulations on Carriage of Passengers and Baggage  In respect of Domestic Passengers;  Warsaw Convention, and Hague Convention amending this convention shall be applicable to the domestic flights, and such conventions shall set out the responsibility of the carrier for death, injury and loss of baggage or damage to baggage, and shall restrict the same in many cases.  1.   The phrase “Ticket” used in this convention means the passenger tickets and baggage coupons, and the terms of convention together with warnings are integral parts of the ticket; the “Warsaw Convention” means the Convention signed in Warsaw on 12.10.1929 for the unification of certain rules relating to international carriage by air and The Hague Convention of 28.09.1955 amending this convention ( DK.21.073 The Warsaw Convention, Signed On 12 October 1929, and The Protocol To Amend The  Warsaw Convention (The Hague Protocol)/Chapter 1—Passenger Ticket).  2.   Pursuant to the Turkish Civil Aviation Law dated 14.10.1983 and numbered 2920 (DK.21.015 Turkish Civil Aviation Law Numbered  2920/Part 4.   Responsibilities under the Carriage Contract ), such carriage shall be based on the regulations and restrictions regarding the responsibility of the carrier, set out in the abovementioned Law, Warsaw Convention, and The Hague Convention amending this convention ( DK.21.073 The Warsaw Convention, Signed On 12 October 1929, and The Protocol To Amend The Warsaw Convention  (The Hague Protocol)/Chapter 2—Carriage Documents).  3.   Unless to the contrary of the matters stated above; carriage and other services of the carrier are subject to the provisions of this ticket, applicable fare tariffs, carriage conditions of the carrier that are integral part of this convention and regulations of the same regarding these conditions  4.   The regulations releasing or restricting the liabilities of the carrier are implemented for the benefit of carrier’s agencies, employees, and representatives as well. In respect of the International Passengers; Warning:   Travel of passengers may be subject to Montreal Convention or Warsaw Convention system, and such conventions may restrict the obligations of the airline companies in cases of death or physical injuries, loss of baggage, damage to baggage and delays.  1.   The phrase "Ticket" used in this agreement shall mean the passenger tickets and baggage vouchers, or the vouchers containing travel details in case of issuance of electronic ticket; and terms and conditions of the agreement together with the notes shall constitute the integral parts of the ticket; and the "carriage" shall mean "transportation"; and the "carrier" shall mean all air carriers, which carry or assume the responsibility for carrying the passengers or their baggage, or which provide any other services regarding carriage, pursuant to this agreement. The “Warsaw Convention” means the Convention signed in Warsaw on 12.10.1929 for the unification of certain rules relating to international carriage by air and The Hague Convention of 28.09.1955 amending this convention (DK.21.073  The   Warsaw   Convention,   Signed   On   12   October   1929,   and   The   Protocol   To   Amend   The   Warsaw   Convention   (The   Hague  Protocol)/Chapter 1—Passenger Ticket), and the regulations of the applicable one shall prevail.  2.   Such carriage shall be subjected to the regulations and restrictions, which have been set out by the Warsaw Convention, and which are related to the responsibility; however, this principle shall not be applicable in the event that such carriage is not an international carriage, defined by the Warsaw Convention.  3.   Unless contrary to the matters stated above, the carriage and any other services provided by the carrier shall be subject to; The provisions of this ticket, Applicable fare tariffs, Conditions of carriage that constitute a part of this agreement, and the regulations regarding such conditions (These may be seen at the offices of the carrier when applied to). However; in the event that carriage is performed between any station in the United States of America or Canada and any station located in any country other than such countries, then the lists of renumeration, which are applicable in such countries, shall be applied.  4.   The abbreviation of the name of the carrier may be specified on the ticket due to the fact that the full name and abbreviation of the name of the carrier are available in the fare tariffs, conditions of carriage, regulations and operations schedules of the carrier. The station of departure available on the ticket opposite the first abbreviation of the name of carrier shall be considered as the address of the carrier. The intermediate stations, which are available on such tickets, or which are specified as the scheduled travel route of the passenger on operations schedules are the planned intermediate stations. In the event that such carriage is performed by more than one successive carrier, then it shall be considered to be only one carriage process.  5.   Any air carrier, issuing tickets for the flights of any other air carrier, shall carry out such process only through the agent of the other carrier. EK.10.15.001 Security Program/12.2.3.   Bomb Threat/article 12.2.3. Implementation. In case of detection of any bomb on board the aircraft, or in case of any threat call stating that flight security is in danger, then;  a.   In the event that the bomb threat call has been performed by telephone, then such threat call shall be recorded in detail. The voice and behaviors of the person, reporting the threat call, as well as the voices at the background, if any, shall be detected and noted down.  b.   The incident shall be immediately reported to the security units.  c.   In the event that the passengers are on board the aircraft, then passengers and flight crew members shall be disembarked from the aircraft immediately together with the registered baggage, mails and cargo.  d.   The aircraft shall be towed to any distant and isolated area of the airport with the purpose of keeping any damage to the life and property in case of any possible explosion, at the minimum level.  e.   Air traffic service shall be informed about the matter, and it shall be ensured that air traffic and ground traffic shall be carried out at any area away from the incident site in a safe manner.  f.   The baggage, cargo and loads shall be carried to an area, which they will not cause damage to terminal building, facilities and any other aircraft, in order to be investigated by the security officers and the bomb squad. Note: Checked passenger baggage is the baggage that is loaded into the hold of the same aircraft and shipped. For some reasons, cabin baggage can also be checked and shipped as registered baggage in the aircraft hold. (Article 1.1.6. Baggage Acceptance)  2.2.2. Personnel (Employee) Roles  In this section, the employee involved in the baggage activities are mentioned. Depending on the size and structure of the baggage operation at the relevant airport, different employee and groups may take part in the operation.. Baggage Services Operations Management Staff: It is the staff responsible for supervising and managing the performance of the operation as well as making the decisions. Baggage Services Operations Control Staff: It is the staff responsible for planning baggage operations and meeting criteria, including the reshipment of short-connected and unconnected baggage, to ensure smooth baggage operation. Baggage Services Operations Staff: It is the staff responsible from the baggage segregation area to transferring and matching the baggage to the aircraft and from unloading to delivery to the passenger. Furthermore, they do not allow unauthorized employee (without a card/entry permit) to enter the zone. . Aircraft Loading Employee: It is the staff responsible for loading and unloading baggage from the aircraft. Furthermore, they do not allow unauthorized employee (without a card/entry permit) to enter the zone.  2.3. Safe Baggage Handling  It is important that all employees are aware of all the rules and risks related to baggage handling, and that they are properly trained and follow the guidelines below as a minimum to ensure their health and safety.  a.   Handling techniques 1. Baggage handling requires the employee to manually perform activities such as pushing and pulling non-powered ground equipment (baggage trolley, ULD) and heavy baggage. 2. Baggage employee must always be aware of the best lifting techniques to reduce the risk of injury when handling baggage. 3. For manual usage techniques, see   DK.41.012 Airport Handling Manual (AHM)/462 Article 4.5.3. Safe Operating Practices in Aircraft Handling.  b.   The baggage employee must not lift more than his physical strength to avoid injury.  c.   In order to ensure that the employee is not injured while carrying the baggage, s/he must ensure that proper care is taken in terms of health and safety and, if possible, use assistive devices to carry heavy loads.  d.   It is necessary to ensure that appropriate personal protective equipment is available and used.  e.   It is necessary to make sure that the baggage handling is done properly. (Baggage must be put, not thrown, on the conveyor.)  f.   When using a baggage trolley and a dolly, the safety precautions in article 3.1.3.3. Non-Motorized Ground Support Equipment must be observed.  g.   Make sure that vehicles such as baggage trolley, tractor and dolly are disconnected and connected, and that no one is working between or near them during the maneuver.  Danger:  Be very careful with your hands, fingers and feet when transporting and tying baggage trolleys or carts to the tractor or other equipment. Always use the rig lever and never the towing ring. Ask for help if necessary.  2.3.1. Baggage Security  The registered baggage is subjected to security check at the points where it is accepted in or outside the airport. The baggage subjected to security scanning is stored in a place where it is protected against unauthorized access until it is loaded to the relevant flight. After acceptance of the baggage, security measures (surveillance by employee, CCTV, etc.) are taken during storage to prevent unauthorized access to or placement of prohibited articles in the baggage. Equipment such as baggage trolleys and ULDs in the necessary quantity. 3. Operations of special baggage belonging to the flight. 4. Appointment of employee for the delivery of baggage to the flight or the designated area (4.5.6.2. Carrying the Load).  b.   Connection baggage from arrivals to departure flights is reviewed: 1. It is determined from which arrival flights that baggage is expected for the departure flight. 2. Determined arrival flights are monitored in order to make connections. 3. Short connection baggage is planned for baggage handling system or board-to-board operation.  c.   The parking position of the departure flight is reviewed for timely delivery of baggage: 1. The time of dispatch to the parking area is determined for departure. 2. The status of the parking position is determined for holding and loading the baggage or for additional security measures. 3. It is necessary to consider the methods of protection against the adverse weather conditions and extremely hot weather.  d.   Special equipment is planned, if needed, for the handling of cargo such as weapons, live animals, and vehicles of passengers with reduced mobility, and informed to the relevant employee.  2.4.2.
